note: Informal eureka list (created 2026-10-10). N3 candidates that cannot enter the Lean shortlist (data/eureka_shortlist.json) because the item has no Lean declarations behind a comparator. They are graded with the same N-tests at text level; discoverability (test 4) and downstream speedup can only be run informally (LLM judge, pen-and-paper), so none of them can become a confirmed eureka step. An item moves to the Lean shortlist if it is later formalized. Untiered: the five 2026-10-09 items keep their old tier for reference only.

items.item: Counterexample witnesses: coupled-pencil fourfold with local dihedral labels; genus-0 Eisenstein surface family (Shafarevich)
items.for: Refutes Shafarevich's conjecture in dimension 2 and in Kollár's large-π₁ form. Witness profile like 047: small objects with opposing constraints. No model-produced precedent.
items.against: No Lean; the relations and path lemmas are terse; the fourfold's π₁ must be non-linear, which the paper understates.
items.next_test: Expert review of the fourfold lemmas; test 4 with the route given vs withheld.
items.why_informal: No Lean formalization of the family.

items.item: Flux pair (h, Z) plus universal tensor certificate (critical dimension d* = 7, one-phase Bernoulli)
items.for: Would close d* = 7 and implicitly settle a stability conjecture for cones in dimensions 5 and 6.
items.against: The Lean formalizes none of the new mathematics, only the known 2009 example. It rests on a 1,714-key Python certificate the paper admits is not tied to its formulas; the margins are tight (0.99992). It may be a variant of Jerison–Savin's Hessian test.
items.next_test: Independently re-derive and re-check the certificate before any novelty test.
items.why_informal: The family's Lean (BernoulliCone) formalizes only the known De Silva–Jerison example, none of the new mathematics; the item is not in Lean.

items.item: Guard-pinned wall realization for p > 2 (Ball–Evans approximation in 3D)
items.for: Solves a problem Hencl's survey lists as open; no precedent found for the device.
items.against: Everything around it is classical (Kirby torus trick, Federer–Fleming, Moreau, Väisälä); it may read as routine assembly. About 15k unreviewed lines, no Lean.
items.why_informal: No Lean formalization of the family.

items.item: Value-space renormalization iteration (bi-Lipschitz coordinates at regular RCD points)
items.for: Resolves a conjecture going back to Cheeger–Colding 1997; provenance clean.
items.against: Nearest neighbour is the cited David–Toro patch construction; a judge may read it as David–Toro plus a Newton step. No Lean.
items.next_test: Test 4 with directional pinching and mass forms given.
items.why_informal: No Lean formalization of the family.

items.item: Entropy-excess potential with transport inequalities (Sogge local smoothing in 3+1)
items.for: Claims all of Sogge's 3+1 conjecture, with Bochner–Riesz, restriction and Kakeya corollaries.
items.against: Lowest confidence in the random batch. Family 074 (a day earlier, same release) uses the same entropy/extremal architecture, so it looks like a reused method. About 12.6k unreviewed lines, no Lean.
items.next_test: Compare with family 074 first; expert review.
items.why_informal: No Lean formalization of the family.

items.item: Real-component detector Theta at p=2 (BSD formula, Selmer coranks 0 and 1)
items.for: Passes tests 1 and 2 as far as checked, and is a knockout for a necessary branch (test 3 borderline on share). Paper itself flags it as 'the new ingredient'. Low confidence: searches were snippet-level, real points of modular curves are a classical topic, and the device serves one residual sub-case at p=2 (limited downstream reach, so a downstream speedup is unlikely). Correctness of the Hecke eigenlaw at branch points is unchecked. Falls to N2 if an expert identifies a known Hecke-equivariant real-component functional (e.g. in Mazur/Ribet component-group theory).

test3.verdict: borderline: knockout for a necessary branch, small DAG share
test3.evidence: It is the only primitivity input for the real-S3 residual case of the 2-part (one of four residual branches; M3 Sec 13 is ~1,100 of 9,051 lines, ~5% of the family). Without it the headline fails for curves whose E[2] has image S3 with real quadratic sign field. Fails the 20% share proxy; passes as a knockout.

items.item: Adjoint positivity of the entire highest Hodge line on the full-period quotient, via strict rank loss on boundary and ramification divisors
items.F: F3 (auxiliary base S built to drive the proof) + F5 (replaces b-semiampleness/abundance of the moduli part by an adjoint-bigness statement on a different base)
items.pivot_distance: no trace. Estimated >= 2 from L + the classical reduction: (a) choose S = full period image (where BC applies) rather than the image of the line map or the Iitaka base of M; (b) formulate and prove strict rank loss nu(L|D_i) < nu(L) on N != 0 and finite-inertia divisors. About 1 if the C1 statement is given (volume subtraction is then routine).
items.for: No statement found in any field giving adjoint bigness K_S + jL of a possibly non-big Hodge line on the full period image with boundary and ramification absorbed; BFMT and Ambro give stronger conclusions only under the generic-effectiveness hypothesis that the Iitaka kappa(F)=0 case violates. Every ingredient is named prior art (BC, BBT, BFMT, Andre, Bakker-Tsimerman Ax-Schanuel, CKS, Siu-type volume subtraction): the candidate is their problem-specific coupling, not a transfer. Downgrade risks: (i) an expert shows BFMT's CY-Hodge-bundle conditions hold for root-cover VHS (=> N1 corollary); (ii) a boundary-absorption statement exists in the hyperbolicity literature (Brunebarbe 2020, BFMT Secs. 5-6, 2608.22682: not read in full); (iii) the ~1000-line rank-loss proof is wrong (then the item is void, not merely downgraded); (iv) discoverability arm B hits. Confidence is lower than 322/287 …
items.against: D2 if any of: (a) an expert (e.g. Bakker, Filipazzi, Mauri, Tsimerman, Ambro, Fujino, Brunebarbe) shows BFMT's CY-Hodge-bundle semiampleness conditions (integrable, torsion combinatorial monodromy) hold for least-index root-cover VHS of kappa=0 fibres with negative generic sub-boundary, making C1 a corollary; (b) a boundary-absorption statement K + jL big for a lower-rank Hodge line appears in BFMT Secs. 5-6, Brunebarbe 2020 or arXiv:2608.22682 (none read in full); (c) P-C1 arm B shows contamination-controlled models propose the full-period base + rank-loss route at the calibrated rate. The family claims collapse (not merely downgrade) if the ~1000-line rank-loss proof fails.
